result.title: Learning What Pairs Miss for Higher-Order Multimodal Alignment
result.summary: Contrastive learning beyond two modalities now scores the whole tuple with multilinear products, volumes, and fusion heads, critics that can represent the joint distribution. In practice these critics still behave like bags of pairs. Their negatives break at least two of the three pairs, a single pairwise check rejects them, and when most samples can be solved by pairs the higher-order term receives almost no gradient. To solve this problem, we propose CHORD (Contrastive Higher-Order Residuals with Decoys), which trains a residual against decoys drawn from a calibrated pairwise model, negatives that the pairwise model finds plausible, so that rejecting them often needs all three modalities. Drawing decoys costs one inner-product query over a memory bank, and the optimal residual is the log-ratio between the data and the pairwise model, so the decoy loss also bounds what that model misses. On M3-Mix, where one in ten training samples needs all three modalities, our CHORD improves accuracy on those samples by 21.2 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines. CHORD also gives the best two-to-one results on every real dataset, and its residual improves other retrievers without retraining.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CHORD，针对多模态对比学习中的「成对得分」缺陷，以校准的成对模型生成负样本诱饵并学习高阶残差，使三模态联合判别真正依赖所有模态，并在多模态对齐与检索任务上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以残差衡量成对模型遗漏的高阶交互，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否仅凭成对关系即可被使用、以及内部表示是否保留任务必需的多实体联合信息；但论文不涉及推理期状态生成，属于方法线索借鉴。
